prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Pasadena, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1467; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you please state and spell your full name for the record?

A: Sure. It's the name on my policy, and I can spell it if you need me to.

Q: That's fine, we already have it on file. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection?

A: I was making a left turn at a signalized intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The light was green for me, or it had just turned to a green arrow. I started into the turn when a vehicle coming from the opposite direction hit the front driver's side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I glanced up and saw headlights, but I was focused on getting through the intersection. By the time I registered it, it was already on me.

Q: How fast do you estimate you were traveling when you started the turn?

A: Very slow, maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour. I was basically creeping through the turn.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Where did you first feel pain or notice an injury?

A: My left wrist hit the steering wheel and the door frame when the airbag went off. I felt it right away, and it swelled up quickly. I went to the emergency room later that day, and they told me it was fractured.

Q: Have you received any follow-up treatment since then?

A: I've had a cast put on, and I have an orthopedic appointment scheduled. I'm also having trouble gripping things for work.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add before we finish?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get this resolved so I can get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. We'll be in touch with next steps. Have a good day.

A: You too. Thanks.
